marks.named: a Frogger or Freeway-style cross-the-board game
marks.conclusion: A policy or value network for an 8x8 walled grid game, read as a Frogger/Freeway-style crossing game with agent at the bottom. It leaves the channel and output meanings unconfirmed.
marks.judge_notes: Board: upside-down (SHEET.md), so I marked against that column: agent row 1, ball rows 2-8, bricks rows 6-8, border always on, previous frame rows 1-8. The reply's footprints match that column exactly (ch0 row 1 only; ch1 rows 2-8; ch2 rows 6-8; ch4 rows 1-8), and it finds the always-on border via the bias-clone rows. It gets the meanings wrong. It calls ch0 a top-row goal/spawn, ch2 the agent (bottom), and ch1/ch4 lane obstacles. Only ch3 (wall) earns a meaning point. Layout 1/2: the footprints are right but attached to the wrong kinds of thing. RULING (orientation bonus): I gave 0. The reply reads the numbers on the turned board correctly but not the board, since it puts the agent at the bottom and so reads a different game. It never says orientation is a convention. If the user counts footprint-correct as 'reads the board correctly', this would be 1. Name: Freeway is the wrong game here, so 0. Actions 1/5: it says the outputs are the usual five grid-world actions, but gives no mapping for them. It notes that 0-2 move together and 3/4 oppose, as read from W3 alone, and says nothing about left/right or about outputs doing nothing. Depth 1 (first layer plus W3 alone). Activation: 'ReLU is the likely guess', so 0. No deductions: every wrong semantic claim is hedged ('looks like', 'consistent with', 'would also fit'). Its 'a Frogger or Freeway-style game' is a hedged best guess.
